title: Original-paper evidence for output sharing: Zhang and Jung GBDT-MO

paper.title: GBDT-MO: Gradient Boosted Decision Trees for Multiple Outputs

derivation.claim: One partition q(x) maps each input to a leaf whose value is a d-dimensional vector.
Second-order leaf objective with L2 penalty: exact w*=−(ΣH_i+λI)^−1Σg_i; optimum−0.5Gᵀ(H+λI)^−1G.
For diagonalH, w_j=−G_j/(H_j+λ), optimum−0.5ΣG_j²/(H_j+λ); split improves total across outputs.

Scaled diagonal upper-bound condition γH_ii≥Σ_j|H_ij|; omitted Taylor remainder; scaled diagonal solution and discussion of rescaling learning rate/λ. Not an unconditional guarantee for arbitrary suppliedH.
Authors explicitly consider only subsets of outputs correlated and proposeL0 sparse leaves; this is not independent partitions nor a current hypothesis adoption.

balanced_findings.claim: Shared structures interpreted as indirect regularization; synthetic and classification curves show slower/lower training fit but improved test behavior in studied conditions.
Paper explicitly admits slower convergence, especially early training.
Yeast TableV:XGBoost62.94% versusMO62.29%;TableXII reported confidence MO>XGBoost0.067.
Student-por MO0.24392 versusSO0.24408RMSE;TableXII reported confidence MO better thanSO0.561. Do not call this a conventional statistically significant universal advantage.
Independent partitions relax common-cut restrictions and may reduce training fit error; extra flexibility can fit output-specific noise and remove sharing regularization.
No controlled sweep from compatible to antagonistic output partitions and no solarwind multihorizon forecasting task; negative transfer is not directly quantified.
